findings.claim: Endpoint-coordinate effects are dominated by shape (second-moment) descriptors rather than centroid translation: shape_yy shows the strongest integrated high-low contrast (z=-0.513, q=1.5e-05, positive_batch_fraction=0.0), with shape_xx (z=-0.495, q=8.1e-04) and shape_zz (z=-0.183, q=0.067) weaker but same-signed.

Centroid translation contrasts are largely unsupported: global_centroid_x (z=-0.111, q=0.257) and global_centroid_z (z=-0.061, q=0.481) are null, while global_centroid_y is the only centroid term with a small significant negative effect (z=-0.243, q=0.0136, positive_batch_fraction=0.214).

Continuous contrast functions over the observed window are non-monotone and time-conditioned: landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z=+9.27 and last_rate_z=-10.00, and landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z=-72.4 and last_rate_z=+5.5, so a constant rule is not supported by the observed-node linear fits.

Several local-derivative features carry strong sign conflicts (landmark_00_local_dx: 9 strong_sign_conflicts, 6 sign changes; landmark_00_local_dz: 7 strong_sign_conflicts, 10 sign changes), indicating unstable direction evidence rather than a coherent marginal descriptor.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control, and the observed score window is [0.0,0.5] with curve support [0.0,0.49]; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so these coordinate contrasts are not absolute affinity benefits.

hypotheses.falsifier: shape_yy or shape_xx integrated contrast loses significance or reverses sign under multiplicity adjustment in an independent batch set.
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: Shape (second-moment) coordinate contrasts, especially shape_yy and shape_xx, are the most coherent joint coordinate signal and would be the priority direction over centroid translation.

hypotheses.falsifier: validated fits show no rate sign change or the observed-node interpolation is not reproducible.
hypotheses.observable: observed-node linear rate of landmark contrast features
hypotheses.scope: observed score nodes only, no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule is better supported than a constant rule because landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy change rate sign within the observed window.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data were supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Descendant survival/quality credit, turnover residual accounting, joint covariance/mode diagnostics and uncertainty-ranked multiplicity comparisons were not read in this turn; those comparisons remain unavailable rather than resolved.
Continuous-trend rows report observed-node linear fits with extrapolation_allowed=false; no extrapolation beyond the observed window is warranted.
Coordinate contrasts are geometric descriptors, not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation.
